title: Comparisons, Conditionals, and Logic
summary: Turn comparisons into booleans, use if/else to choose a path, and combine requirements with logical operators.

sketchBlocks.title: Comparisons produce booleans
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A **comparison** asks JavaScript a yes-or-no question and produces a boolean result. For an event, one useful question is whether any seats remain:

```js
const seatsRemaining = 4;
console.log(seatsRemaining > 0);
```

Line by line:

1. `const seatsRemaining = 4;` stores the current seat count.
2. `seatsRemaining > 0` asks whether that count is greater than zero.
3. `console.log(...)` shows the boolean result, which is `true` for this example.

You can also compare values for exact equality with `===` or inequality with `!==`. Prefer these strict comparison operators in this course so JavaScript does not quietly convert one type into another while comparing.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Choose what the program should do
sketchBlocks.title: if/else turns a boolean into a decision
Combine boolean rules with &&, ||, and !
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Real decisions often depend on more than one fact. Registration should be open only when seats remain **and** the deadline has not passed:

```js
const seatsRemaining = 5;
const deadlinePassed = false;
const isOpen = seatsRemaining > 0 && !deadlinePassed;

console.log(isOpen);
```

Line by line:

1. `seatsRemaining` stores the current seat count.
2. `deadlinePassed` stores whether the deadline is already over.
3. `seatsRemaining > 0 && !deadlinePassed` checks both rules and stores the combined boolean in `isOpen`.
4. `console.log(isOpen);` shows whether registration is open under those two rules.

`&&` means **both conditions must be true**. The first condition checks for seats. `!deadlinePassed` flips `false` to `true`, so it means “the deadline has not passed.”

Use `||` when either condition is enough. Use `!` when you need the opposite of a boolean value. Keep the expression close to the rule you would say out loud.

quizDraft.title: Choose the matching rule
quizDraft.prompt: Registration should open only when seats remain and the deadline has not passed. Which expression matches that rule?
quizDraft.hint: The word “and” means both requirements must pass.

help.hint_1: Start with the comparison that checks whether seats remain.
help.hint_2: Then combine it with “deadline has not passed” using `&&`.

quizDraft.title: Recognize closed-registration cases
quizDraft.prompt: Which situations should make registration closed? Select all that apply.
quizDraft.hint: The open rule requires seats remaining and a deadline that has not passed.

help.hint_1: If either required condition fails, the registration cannot be open.
help.hint_2: No seats and a passed deadline each break one requirement.

quizDraft.title: Complete the open-registration condition
quizDraft.prompt: Choose the logical operator that requires both conditions to pass.
quizDraft.hint: Choose the operator whose result is true only when both sides are true.

help.hint_1: One choice succeeds when either side is true; this rule needs the stricter behavior.
help.hint_2: Test one false side mentally: the whole registration condition should then be false.

quizDraft.title: Follow an if/else decision
quizDraft.prompt: Arrange the steps JavaScript follows for an if/else statement.
quizDraft.hint: JavaScript must know whether the condition is true before it chooses a branch.

help.hint_2: Exactly one branch runs, then execution continues after the conditional.

quizDraft.title: Check whether inventory is empty
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: An inventory screen needs to know whether there are no items left so it can decide what state to show next. Task: Create `isEmpty` by checking whether `itemsLeft` is exactly 0, then log the boolean result. Expected result: the Console shows `true` only when inventory is empty.
quizDraft.hint: This task needs an equality comparison that produces true or false.

help.concept: A comparison produces a boolean value.
help.hint_2: Use strict equality and assign the result to `isEmpty` before logging it.

quizDraft.title: Choose a membership message
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: An access screen must show a different message for members and guests instead of displaying the same text to everyone. Task: Use `if/else` with `isMember`. Assign `"Member access"` when it is true and `"Guest access"` otherwise, then log `accessMessage`. Expected result: the Console shows the message that matches the current membership state.
quizDraft.hint: Let the boolean choose between two message assignments.

help.concept: An if/else statement chooses one of two paths from a boolean condition.
help.hint_2: Assign one message inside `if` and the other inside `else`, then log `accessMessage` afterward.

quizDraft.title: Check whether a book can be borrowed
quizDraft.prompt: Problem: A library cannot allow a loan just because someone has a card; the borrower must also have no overdue book. Task: Create `canBorrow`. It should be true only when `hasLibraryCard` is true and the borrower does not have an overdue book. Log the result. Expected result: the Console shows the combined borrowing decision.

help.concept: Logical AND combines requirements; negation flips a boolean condition.
help.hint_1: Start with `hasLibraryCard && ...` because both rules are required.
